re_line: Lai's Double Ten address and Chinese drills, militia boat off Taiwan's east coast, EU cap on Chinese hybrids, China-Laos base, espionage case in Los Angeles
editors_note: This is the second China Room Brief. It arrives every Tuesday with a recap of the past week in U.S.-China relations and a look ahead.

heard_on_the_hill.headline: Three senators cite spy case as CCP surveillance export
heard_on_the_hill.body: Republican Senators Blackburn, Ricketts and Scott called the case against Zhang Wanying evidence that the CCP is exporting repressive surveillance to the U.S., VOA Chinese reported. The FBI arrested Zhang at Los Angeles International Airport on October 4 on a charge of acting as an unregistered agent of the Chinese government, alleging she surveilled the son of Taiwan President Lai Ching-te. China's foreign ministry said it was unaware of the case.

heard_on_the_hill.headline: Moolenaar seeks review of Hong Kong's Fed liquidity access
heard_on_the_hill.body: House Select Committee on the CCP Chairman John Moolenaar called for a review of Hong Kong's access to a Federal Reserve liquidity facility, a request CNBC set against China's promotion of the renminbi as a global reserve currency.
heard_on_the_hill.event: Hong Kong Fed liquidity access review

heard_on_the_hill.headline: Select Committee faults Webull over China links
heard_on_the_hill.body: A bipartisan Select Committee on China investigation led by Chairman John Moolenaar and Ranking Member Ro Khanna found that brokerage Webull Financial "has not been transparent about its links to China." Webull shares fell after the committee flagged the ties, Reuters reported.

heard_on_the_hill.headline: Bennet among U.S. lawmakers visiting Taiwan
heard_on_the_hill.body: Several U.S. lawmakers are visiting Taiwan after last month's Trump-Xi summit, VOA Chinese reported, with AIT saying the visits reinforce the U.S.-Taiwan partnership. Senator Michael Bennet is meeting senior officials on regional security this week. Defense Minister Wellington Koo said he had not heard of plans to split a prospective $14 billion arms sale into smaller packages.

in_the_news.headline: Lai says Taiwan will not give up its freedom; Beijing calls him 'pragmatic independence worker'
in_the_news.body: Lai Ching-te told Double Ten crowds that Taiwan "cherishes peace" but will not give up its freedom, the Washington Post reported, and pledged NT$1.1 trillion ($34.5 billion) for defense in 2027. The U.S. welcomed his commitment to Taiwan Strait stability. Beijing's Taiwan Affairs Office called him a "pragmatic Taiwan independence worker," and live-fire drills across four seas run October 12-20.

in_the_news.event: Chinese militia boat off Taiwan's east coast
in_the_news.headline: China militia boat spotted for first time off Taiwan's east coast
in_the_news.body: A Taiwanese patrol spotted a Chinese maritime militia boat off Taiwan's east coast for the first time, Reuters reported, a new area for craft usually seen near the Taiwan Strait median line. Taipei Times identified it as the Minfudingyu 07902, sailing with a coast guard cutter and a research vessel in mid-August. A State Department spokesperson said the patrols "only exacerbate tensions."

in_the_news.headline: China, EU step back from trade war with limits on hybrid car exports
in_the_news.body: At 350,000 units a year, the EU's new cap on Chinese hybrid imports followed talks between Maroš Šefčovič and Commerce Minister Wang Wentao in Beijing on October 8-9, Bloomberg reported. The New York Times said the deal could roughly halve hybrid shipments over four years. MOFCOM said it secures China's continued "export space" in Europe.

in_the_news.headline: China expands military reach with new base in Laos
in_the_news.body: China is building a military facility with a new runway at Ban Keun, Laos, the New York Times reported. Reuters satellite imagery showed attack aircraft and military vehicles at the site, while an analysis in The Diplomat counted eight Chinese training aircraft and described a joint support center that opened September 29, not an attack base.

in_the_news.event: U.S. disruption of Integrity Tech hacking
in_the_news.headline: U.S. moves to disrupt hacking infrastructure tied to China's Integrity Tech
in_the_news.body: The U.S. said it is working to disrupt hacking infrastructure it attributes to China's Integrity Tech Group, and the FBI confirmed it seized tools used in the operation, Reuters reported. Foreign ministry spokeswoman Mao Ning urged Washington to "abandon double standards."

research_roundup.event: Chinese research vessels near undersea cables
research_roundup.headline: China’s Weaponization of Dual-Use Research Vessels for Undersea Data Dominance
research_roundup.body: Jose M. Macias III, Tao-Hung Chang, Nico Vacca and Benjamin Jensen analyze 223 vessels and find that Chinese research ships spend an unusually large share of time near subsea infrastructure on the high seas. They call for stronger allied monitoring, coordinated patrols and faster cable repair.

research_roundup.event: PLA lessons from Ukraine drone war
research_roundup.headline: Learning Without Bleeding: China’s Lessons from the Russia-Ukraine Drone War
research_roundup.body: Lilly Min-Chen Lee and Kateryna Bondar trace how quickly Chinese analysts identify battlefield innovations and how the PLA turns those lessons into training, procurement, hardware and force structure.

research_roundup.headline: Russia’s Turn to China Under Sanctions: Sanctions Decay, Substitution Elasticity, and the Challenge of Sustaining Pressure
research_roundup.body: Damien Spleeters argues that sanctions lose force not only when governments stop updating them, but also when targeted actors replace restricted products, suppliers and acquisition channels faster than controls can adapt.

research_roundup.headline: Understanding the Chinese-Language Media Landscape in Southeast Asia
research_roundup.body: Lauren Mai, Andreyka Natalegawa, Gregory B. Poling and Japhet Quitzon argue that countering Chinese information warfare requires buy-in from regional partners and awareness of the scale, scope and impact of Chinese-language media in Southeast Asia.

research_roundup.headline: The AI Export Dilemma
research_roundup.body: William Alan Reinsch weighs whether the United States should allow exports of AI technologies and what strategies it could use to stay ahead in the global technology race.
